opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: fast and almost always correct
opinions.quote: [With DS-flash,] there's something to be said for the speed with which it gets word done - I take fewer "it's compiling" breaks… What's crazy is that the speedy work it does is pretty much always correct

opinions.name: DeepSeek Harness
opinions.point: pairing with DS flash almost too good to be true
opinions.quote: This speed & good-work combo is the DS signature IMO… For my harness, Deepseek Harness + DS-4-1-flash combo is almost too good to be true

opinions.name: OpenCode Go/Zen
opinions.point: best value; five-hour limit lasts far longer
opinions.quote: I subscribe to OpenCode Go… It's by far the best value since it's only $10 and I doesn't run out of its five hour limit in an hour they way Claude Code/Codex do.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: nothing to complain about at work
opinions.quote: At work, I'm using Codex with the subscription they give me, and I don't really have anything to complain about.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: desktop app much more useful than command line
opinions.quote: If I'm using Codex or Claude directly, I'm using the desktop apps. The apps are MUCH more useful than doing everything on the command line now.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: desktop app much more useful than command line
opinions.quote: If I'm using Codex or Claude directly, I'm using the desktop apps. The apps are MUCH more useful than doing everything on the command line now.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: limits suffice now but tighten with more agents
opinions.quote: I just about make it under the $200 Claude plan limits though as I add more and more agents, that's going to get uncomfortable.

opinions.name: Conductor
opinions.point: poor support for multiple repos in one session
opinions.quote: [With Conductor,] the annoying part is that if I have a frontend repository and a backend repository I have to tell each session "talk to this workspace to adapt the backend"… I wish they had better support for multiple repos in one session.

opinions.name: Amp
opinions.point: very polished, but diff reading not prominent
opinions.quote: I'm evaluating https://ampcode.com/ which is very polished, but I feel like the diff-reading part is not very prominent there which I find a bit odd.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: sessions message each other, replacing orchestration tools
opinions.quote: Claude Code (and Codex too I believe?) can message other sessions these days… This has removed most of that back and forth for me and eliminated the need for orchestration tools.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: supreme intelligence when needed
opinions.quote: Codex $100- daily driver… Claude $20- gives me the supreme intelligence for when I need it.

opinions.name: CodeBuddy
opinions.point: excellent, variety of models, amazing value
opinions.quote: Codebuddy pro about $10 Excellent for free and a variety of models and amazing value.

opinions.name: Grok bot
opinions.point: great for job applications and emails
opinions.quote: Grok bot had a deal on and I got it for like $30 for three months and is shit hot for applications for jobs, emails all kinds of cool shit.

opinions.name: Instinct bot
opinions.point: found better deals than Grok bot
opinions.quote: I use free instinct bot too and I ran it against grok bot to find if it would find better deals and it did most of the time.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: was happy until branch picking for worktrees got harder
opinions.quote: I have personally been using the Claude Code Desktop App and was happy with it until they made it harder to pick a branch for each worktree!

opinions.name: ThinkRail
opinions.point: easy worktrees from any branch, great spec-driven flow
opinions.quote: I tried JetBrains experimental agent IDE, ThinkRail, and I love it! Super easy to start worktrees from any branch and the spec driven development experience they promote is great!

opinions.name: Requesty
opinions.point: try any model easily; dashboard a pleasure to use
opinions.quote: [ThinkRail] also let me connect to Requesty for my hobby projects and with that I can easily try any model, from any provider… thanks to Requesty's super awesome dashboard which is a pleasure to use.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: offloads heavy agent work to Kubernetes; works great
opinions.quote: We also have a framework that lets us launch Claude… in our Kubernetes cluster within a devcontainer. That lets us ship heavy work off to another machine so our laptop is not overloaded with agents. It works great

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: usage limits have gone downhill
opinions.quote: I have had a $20 codex subscription… Codex usage limits have really gone down hill so I also now have a $10 opencode go subscription

opinions.name: OpenCode Go/Zen
opinions.point: cheap access to DeepSeek, a great model
opinions.quote: I also now have a $10 opencode go subscription on which I pretty much just use DeepSeek 4.1 flash. I've found DS to be a great model - probably somewhere just below GPT 6.1 Sol but at a fraction of the price.

opinions.name: Chat UI (web/app)
opinions.point: free, with repo and log access for decisions
opinions.quote: I discuss features with chat gpt (because it's free and it has access to my project's repo, read only view of prod logs etc, so can make informed decisions).

opinions.name: OpenRouter
opinions.point: ZDR and harness freedom, but getting costly
opinions.quote: Exclusively using open router at the moment, mostly on principle around ZDR, and freedom to experiment with harnesses - but financially I'll probably have to compromise on this soon.

opinions.name: Chat UI (web/app)
opinions.point: heavily used but disconnected from agentic setup
opinions.quote: I make a lot of use of open-webui, but it's disjoint from the agentic setup currently - it'd be nice to find a better way to share information/research from it into the agentic sessions.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: refuses some personal tasks
opinions.quote: I often have personal tasks that Claude refuses to do, so I have to use Deepseek-v4.1-flash or GLM-5.3.

opinions.name: Discount provider (unnamed)
opinions.point: two-thirds cheaper, but data probably sold
opinions.quote: I've found a discount provider that offers a 2/3 discount and have migrated to them. The catch is the data is probably sold, but given that it has saved me $300 this past month for non-sensitive work…, the tradeoff is worth it.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: too many unfixed and weird issues
opinions.quote: I used to use OpenCode for my API usage, but there are too many issues which have gone unfixed and too many weird issues that I became tired of working around, so I switched to Oh my Pi.

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: not a fan; may rewire Claude Code instead
opinions.quote: I switched to Oh my Pi. I'm not a fan of it either, so before my next big run with open weights models, I will probably rewire Claude Code to use these Chinese models.

opinions.name: Subagents (built-in)
opinions.point: queuing 200+ subagents, 8 at a time, is sufficient
opinions.quote: Claude Code's subagent feature and workflow (subagents, but queuing up >200, and running 8 at a time) are sufficient for my needs.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: sweet spot when paired with Codex
opinions.quote: Claude ($100) + Codex ($20) seems to be a sweet spot, with Codex being able to generate images and do reviews of Claude's code

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: generates images and reviews Claude's code
opinions.quote: Claude ($100) + Codex ($20) seems to be a sweet spot, with Codex being able to generate images and do reviews of Claude's code

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: 24/7 personal assistant reachable anywhere is worth it
opinions.quote: Hermes. I find at least one 24/7 machine with agent running, that you can reach from anywhere to be worth it. As your personal assistant.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: right balance of capability, cost, availability with Codex
opinions.quote: +1 for Claude $100 paired with Codex $20 - feels like the right balance of capability/cost/availability… right now.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: $20 plan balanced; $200 plan felt wasteful
opinions.quote: +1 for Claude $100 paired with Codex $20 - feels like the right balance… I was a $200 codex plan person not that long ago but Tibo's month of resets made me feel like I was wasting my money

opinions.name: GitHub Copilot
opinions.point: great keep/undo review UI, but YOLO harness pushed
opinions.quote: The Local harness has granular keep/undo and nice interface in general for reviewing changes… Unfortunately the copilot team is trying to force the less capable, more YOLO-mode "copilot" harness on people going forward.

opinions.name: GitHub Copilot
opinions.point: access to best OpenAI and Anthropic models
opinions.quote: I use the Local harness in vs code with a GitHub copilot max plan. Gives access to the best models from OpenAI and Anthropic

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: cloud setup a mess, ignored startup instructions
opinions.quote: I briefly tried to set up codex cloud and it was a mess, not following startup instructions so I gave up.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: simple UI, multiple sessions; sticky defaults annoying
opinions.quote: Claude Code Desktop on Windows: I like it. Simple UI… Multiple sessions, virtual groups for sessions, etc… Some of the default selections tend to stick with what you selected first and I dont like those aspects

opinions.name: OpenRig
opinions.point: new favorite; agent-team software factory is fun
opinions.quote: I flip flop between raw Claude Code and subagents to my new favorite, OpenRig… it's a software factory (I know I'm not gonna need it) but it's fun.

opinions.name: Perplexity
opinions.point: made them feel physically ill
opinions.quote: I evaluated using Perplexity Pro for a while… I find it hard to describe the experience of using Perplexity Pro beyond making me feel physically ill when I used it.

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: minimalist; fits limited local resources
opinions.quote: I switched to Pi from Codex because I liked the minimalist philosophy behind it… Pi was a much better match for the resources I had.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: default prompts ate limited local context
opinions.quote: I was having a hard time getting 100k context with any reasonably useful model. The default prompts of Codex ate into that a lot

opinions.name: Paseo
opinions.point: keeps everything organized in one place
opinions.quote: I use Paseo with Claude + Codex and Opencode Go… Paseo helps keeping everything organized and one place, which is easy to review the process and incrementally improve the things.

opinions.name: Baseten
opinions.point: inconsistent performance and pricing
opinions.quote: I've also tried inference services such as baseten and novita, but wasn't satisfied with inconsistency in performance and pricing.

opinions.name: Novita
opinions.point: inconsistent performance and pricing
opinions.quote: I've also tried inference services such as baseten and novita, but wasn't satisfied with inconsistency in performance and pricing.

opinions.name: Cline
opinions.point: not built for reviewing fast-generated code
opinions.quote: I switched away from Cline + VS Code primarily because code is being generated so fast that I needed to optimize for review.

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: small footprint suits self-hosted models
opinions.quote: Mostly Pi (oh-my-pi for main coding env, bare bone pi for drop in usages). Its small footprint is really important for self hosted models

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: slower, shorter context, but enough for most use
opinions.quote: I'm settling with the Qwen series models… Compared to API providers they are slower and has less context length, but enough for most of my use cases.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: setup keeps getting better with use
opinions.quote: My main personal agentic workflow is hermes… As I continue to use this setup it continues to get better, which is my favourite thing about hermes.

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: great at scraping deals, but browses from datacenter
opinions.quote: [Muse] also does a really good job at scraping churning forums and blogs and has made a few thousand dollars in the last month… Muse's biggest flaw is that it runs it's browser actions from a datacenter

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: one max plan very effective with attention
opinions.quote: If you're willing to spend a modicum of attention/effort looking at what the bots are doing, one max Claude plan with Opus and occasionally Fable is very effective.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: more than enough for personal use
opinions.quote: I have a $20 ChatGPT subscription and a $10 OpenCode Go subscription. This is more than enough for my personal use.

opinions.name: OpenCode Go/Zen
opinions.point: more than enough for personal use
opinions.quote: I have a $20 ChatGPT subscription and a $10 OpenCode Go subscription. This is more than enough for my personal use.

opinions.name: Zed
opinions.point: better agent support, weaker IDE than JetBrains
opinions.quote: I primarily use Zed and JetBrains IDEs (Zed has overall better agent support, JetBrains still has by far the better IDEs).

opinions.name: JetBrains AI / Junie
opinions.point: far better IDE, weaker agent support than Zed
opinions.quote: I primarily use Zed and JetBrains IDEs (Zed has overall better agent support, JetBrains still has by far the better IDEs).

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: Opus codes well but misses the real problem
opinions.quote: I use the Zed IDE with Opus 5.5 pro subscription… [Opus] codes well when you tell it what to do, but it is still dumb about what is the real problem (and so the real solution).

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: now great value; rarely hits weekly limit
opinions.quote: Claude Code with $20 Claude subscription. This used to be a terrible value but now it's a great value, probably because of the IPO. I do a lot of coding and other things and I rarely get close to my weekly limit.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: kept hitting limits, so canceled
opinions.quote: Codex with gpt used to be good value but recently I canceled it cause I kept reaching my limits.

opinions.name: DeepSeek Harness
opinions.point: really great value with DeepSeek API key
opinions.quote: [I also use the] Deepseek harness with a deepseek API key. Really great value.

opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: really great value via DeepSeek harness
opinions.quote: [I also use the] Deepseek harness with a deepseek API key. Really great value.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: many incremental improvements add up to compelling
opinions.quote: My manager described this [custom orchestrator] as incomprehensible lol but it's modeled on conductor but uses Claude code terminal… Many incremental improvements the sum of which are compelling ime

opinions.name: Helyn Implement
opinions.point: process works extremely well; fast iteration
opinions.quote: Helyn Implement for coding, I work on design and specification, agentic protocol handles coding, testing, automated testing, and reviews (multiple models), process works extremely well. Enables fast iteration cycles

opinions.name: Custom assistant
opinions.point: much more flexible than standard harnesses
opinions.quote: most of my interactions now is with claw-like agents hanging off a self-hosted Matrix server in my VPN, and I expect to migrate pretty much all of my use to that setup because it's a lot more flexible.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: nice nonprofit team pricing covers daily work
opinions.quote: We're a non-profit and Anthropic actually has quite nice pricing for teams licenses so I can do most of what I need in a day within the team "Nonprofit Premium" allowances without paying for extra usage.

opinions.name: AWS Bedrock
opinions.point: tracks with AWS spend, working quite well
opinions.quote: For longer batch tasks or our automated systems we're using various models through Bedrock so I can track it with the rest of our AWS spend and that's been working quite well.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: would seem a miracle if Claude Code didn't exist
opinions.quote: If Claude Code didn't exist I would think Opencode was a miracle from heaven so it's a nice backup [if] Anthropic pricing gets unweidy.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: even better than OpenCode, itself excellent
opinions.quote: If Claude Code didn't exist I would think Opencode was a miracle from heaven so it's a nice backup [if] Anthropic pricing gets unweidy.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: coordination layer stops agents stepping on each other
opinions.quote: Hivemind - another one of mine… I get a lot of mileage out of this where file reservations, resource locking etc are concerned. Stops them stepping on each others' toes.

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: screen-free bespoke voice interface; loving it
opinions.quote: [I] made my very own voice interface where I don't even need to look at a screen… So it is bespoke all the way down. Been loving it.

opinions.name: Kokoro
opinions.point: delivers great voice consistency
opinions.quote: I get full claude code, can use the official app for text interface, get to rant and ramble without a screen, and kokoro delivers a great consistency.

opinions.name: OpenChamber
opinions.point: awesome phone app; desktop app has controllable browser
opinions.quote: I've mostly been managing it from my phone - the OpenChamber app is awesome… the desktop OpenChamber app has a built-in browser that it can control, which comes in handy.

opinions.name: Cline
opinions.point: works with local and many providers; great with Claude
opinions.quote: I like using Cline the VS Code extension. It can use local models and local inference with Ollama and tons of external inference providers… It works great with Claude for coding

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: open source grant was quite good
opinions.quote: I previously had an open source grant for Claude and that was quite good as well.

opinions.name: Gemini
opinions.point: products break in unique ways; API needs work
opinions.quote: I don't use Gemini… honestly the thousand moving parts and unique ways in which their products break is annoying… But I think Gemini and the API needs work.

opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: cheap, good, and private via Venice
opinions.quote: My main driver is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, which is cheap, good and (in Venice) private.

opinions.name: Venice
opinions.point: daily credits for any model, privately
opinions.quote: I use Venice.ai with its DIEM token, which gives me daily credits for inference that I can spend on any model at their API prices.

opinions.name: Gemma
opinions.point: feels more street-smart than coding models
opinions.quote: Mostly using Gemma through oMLX, because it feels more street-smart than the more coding focused models

opinions.name: Strata
opinions.point: expert streaming allows running larger models
opinions.quote: experimenting with Qwen-flash-next through Strata, because the streaming of experts really pushes what size of model I can run

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: trusts Anthropic; great mobile remote integration
opinions.quote: Harness: Claude code, mostly, I trust anthropic, and like the remote integration with their mobile app. Being able to say "prototype me this and that ui"… and seeing it and testing it on my phone is awesome.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: easy tooling integrations out of the box
opinions.quote: I want a nice chat interface… that already has basic tooling integrations out of the box. I.e. getting OpenWebUI have search tool was pain. Adding i.e. mcp for my todolist or calendar to Hermes was smooth.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: easy to build; results quite good
opinions.quote: My approach is to build the builder rather than the feature… I feel like the results are quite good too far… Building a custom orchestrator for my workflow was quite easy. Like 1-2 weeks of prompting
